# Implementation-Readiness Checklist: TRACE Phase 1 — F01: Project & Repository Management

**Purpose**: Rigorous requirements-quality and implementation-readiness validation for TRACE Phase 1 (F01: Project & Repository Management), verifying completeness, clarity, testability, security, and architectural alignment before execution.
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context, Phase 0 architecture, and TRACE Constitution principles.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

---

## 1. Project Domain Model

- [x] CHK001 Are the project entity attributes, types, and constraints fully and unambiguously specified (id: UUIDv4, name: 1–100 chars, description: optional text up to 1000 chars, status: ProjectStatus, created_at, updated_at)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK002 Is the `ProjectStatus` lifecycle enumeration explicitly defined with exactly the allowed values (`ACTIVE`, `ARCHIVED`) and valid state transition rules? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-006, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK003 Are project name sanitization and validation rules (e.g., whitespace trimming, empty string rejection, max length bounds) explicitly quantified? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK004 Does the specification define immutability constraints and prohibited operations for projects in `ARCHIVED` status? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, §US1]
- [x] CHK005 Are project reactivation rules specified, including timestamp updates and re-enabling repository registration? [Completeness, Spec §FR-006, §Clarifications]

---

## 2. Repository Domain Model

- [x] CHK006 Are all repository entity attributes, types, and default values explicitly documented (id, project_id, type, location, default_branch, status, last_error, last_validated_at, last_analysis_run_id, created_at, updated_at)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK007 Is the `RepositoryType` enumeration explicitly bounded to `LOCAL` and `REMOTE` without ambiguous placeholder values? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK008 Is the `RepositoryStatus` operational state machine clearly defined with initial state (`REGISTERED`) and transition paths (`CONNECTED`, `ERROR`)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, §FR-025, §FR-026]
- [x] CHK009 Does the specification define the exact behavior and field mutations for `last_error` and `last_validated_at` upon both successful and failed validation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-025, §FR-026]
- [x] CHK010 Is `last_analysis_run_id` explicitly required to be null upon initial registration, reserving analysis linkage strictly for F02? [Traceability, Spec §FR-014, §FR-016]

---

## 3. Project / Repository Relationship & Identity

- [x] CHK011 Is the cardinality between `Project` and `Repository` unambiguously defined as a 1-to-many relationship where every repository belongs to exactly one project? [Clarity, Spec §FR-011, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK012 Are location normalization rules explicitly specified for both local paths (canonical absolute path resolution) and remote URLs (lowercasing scheme/host, stripping trailing `.git` and slashes)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK013 Is repository uniqueness scoped to `(project_id, normalized_location)` so distinct projects can independently register the same repository without collision? [Consistency, Spec §FR-011, §FR-017, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK014 Are repository unregistration/deletion rules explicitly specified, permitting deletion only when `last_analysis_run_id` is null and returning HTTP 409 when linked to analysis runs? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020a, §US2]

---

## 4. PostgreSQL Persistence & Migrations

- [x] CHK015 Is PostgreSQL explicitly specified as the sole authoritative source of application state for projects and repositories? [Traceability, Spec §NFR-001, Constitution §VIII]
- [x] CHK016 Are relational table schemas, column data types, foreign keys, and indexes explicitly defined for `projects` and `repositories` tables? [Completeness, Spec §Key Entities, §NFR-001]
- [x] CHK017 Is the composite unique constraint `uq_project_location (project_id, location)` explicitly specified for the PostgreSQL schema? [Completeness, Spec §FR-017, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK018 Are database schema changes explicitly required to be implemented via an Alembic migration script (`0002_project_repository.py`) chained to the baseline migration? [Traceability, Spec §NFR-002, §Assumptions]
- [x] CHK019 Does the specification require bidirectional Alembic migration capabilities (both `upgrade()` and `downgrade()`)? [Completeness, Spec §NFR-002, Constitution §XV]
- [x] CHK020 Are async SQLAlchemy 2.x session management and rollback requirements on exceptions explicitly specified using `DatabaseGateway`? [Consistency, Spec §NFR-003, Phase 0 Architecture]

---

## 5. Repository Abstraction & Git Provider

- [x] CHK021 Is the `GitProvider` interface specified as a Python Protocol with runtime checkability, decoupling domain services from concrete Git libraries? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, Constitution §XIV]
- [x] CHK022 Are the exact method signatures, argument types, and return value types for `GitProvider` explicitly documented (`validate_local`, `validate_remote`, `detect_default_branch`, `list_remote_references`)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-022, §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK023 Does the specification explicitly prohibit stubbed or unimplemented methods (e.g. `clone`, `diff`) in F01's `GitProvider` to adhere to Constitution §XVII (No Fabricated Implementation State)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK024 Is the `ConnectionValidationResult` value object specified with explicit typed fields (`is_connected: bool`, `detected_branch: str | None`, `error_message: str | None`, `latency_ms: float`)? [Clarity, Spec §Key Entities]
- [x] CHK025 Does the specification define an extensible GitProvider protocol and adapter architecture that allows incremental evolution (adding hosting-specific probe or access capabilities in F02/F04) without breaking existing domain interfaces? [Traceability, Spec §FR-022, Constitution §XIV]

---

## 6. Local Git Repository Validation

- [x] CHK026 Are local repository validation criteria explicitly defined (path existence on host filesystem, process read permissions, `.git` directory presence)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023, §US3]
- [x] CHK027 Does the specification define how bare Git repositories (containing `HEAD`, `refs/`, `objects/` without `.git` subfolder) are validated? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK028 Are relative path traversal bounds and canonical path resolution requirements specified to prevent unauthorized directory access? [Security, Spec §Edge Cases, §NFR-008]
- [x] CHK029 Is default branch resolution behavior for local repositories specified deterministically from the local HEAD symbolic reference? [Clarity, Spec §FR-023, §FR-025]

---

## 7. Remote Git Repository Validation

- [x] CHK030 Is remote repository validation explicitly bounded to non-destructive reference probing (e.g. querying remote refs) without cloning files to disk? [Completeness, Spec §FR-024, §US3]
- [x] CHK031 Are permitted remote repository URL formats explicitly decided, allowing standard schemes (`http://`, `https://`, `ssh://`) and SCP-style SSH syntax (`git@host:org/repo.git`), while strictly rejecting embedded passwords, tokens, or basic-auth credentials? [Clarity, Spec §FR-034]
- [x] CHK032 Is a deterministic network timeout (maximum 10.0 seconds) explicitly mandated for remote validation probes to prevent worker hangs? [Measurability, Spec §FR-028, §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK033 Does the specification define explicit diagnostic failure reasons for remote validation failures (e.g., host unreachable, repository not found, authentication failure)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-026, §US3]
- [x] CHK034 Is the specification clear that remote validation must never fabricate default branch names when the remote HEAD cannot be determined? [Consistency, Spec §FR-027, Constitution §I]

## 8. API Contracts & Endpoint Specifications

- [x] CHK035 Are all 10 F01 RESTful endpoints under `/api/v1` (5 project endpoints and 5 repository endpoints) explicitly documented with HTTP methods, paths, and response codes, clearly distinguished from the Phase 0 `/health` endpoint? [Completeness, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK036 Is the project creation route (`POST /api/v1/projects`) specified with HTTP 201 Created and response schema? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029, §FR-030]
- [x] CHK037 Is the project listing route (`GET /api/v1/projects`) specified with pagination parameters (`limit`, `offset`) and status filtering (`status`)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §FR-029]
- [x] CHK038 Are project archival (`POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/archive`) and reactivation (`POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/activate`) routes specified with idempotent status responses? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029, §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK039 Is repository registration (`POST /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/repositories`) specified under the parent project URI path with HTTP 201 Created? [Consistency, Spec §FR-029]
- [x] CHK040 Is repository listing (`GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/repositories`) specified with response array schema? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019, §FR-029]
- [x] CHK041 Is repository deletion (`DELETE /api/v1/repositories/{repository_id}`) specified with HTTP 204 No Content for unanalyzed repositories? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020a, §FR-029]
- [x] CHK042 Is repository connectivity validation (`POST /api/v1/repositories/{repository_id}/validate`) specified to return HTTP 200 with the validation report regardless of connectivity status? [Clarity, Spec §FR-026, §FR-029]

## 9. Request / Response Schemas & Input Validation

- [x] CHK043 Are strongly typed Pydantic models specified for all request bodies (`ProjectCreateRequest`, `RepositoryRegisterRequest`)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK044 Are strongly typed Pydantic models specified for all response bodies (`ProjectResponse`, `ProjectListResponse`, `RepositoryResponse`, `ValidationReportResponse`)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-030]
- [x] CHK045 Are ISO 8601 UTC timestamp formatting rules (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`) explicitly enforced across all schema fields? [Consistency, Spec §FR-031]
- [x] CHK046 Are string length bounds, null byte prohibitions, and whitespace normalization explicitly declared as Pydantic field validators? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §FR-034]

## 10. Typed Errors & Error Handling

- [x] CHK047 Are domain exceptions explicitly mapped to corresponding HTTP status codes: `ProjectNotFoundError` (404), `ProjectAlreadyExistsError` (409), `ProjectArchivedError` (409), `RepositoryNotFoundError` (404), `DuplicateRepositoryError` (409), `RepositoryInUseError` (409), `InvalidRepositoryLocationError` (422), `UnsupportedRepositoryTypeError` (422), `DatabasePersistenceError` (500)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-033]
- [x] CHK048 Is a standardized error response JSON envelope specified with `error_code`, `message`, and optional `details` dictionary? [Consistency, Spec §FR-032]
- [x] CHK049 Does the specification require error messages to be user-actionable and completely free of sensitive infrastructure details, tokens, or credentials? [Security, Spec §FR-032, §NFR-006]

## 11. Security, Secrets & Credential Isolation

- [x] CHK050 Does the specification strictly forbid storing repository passwords, personal access tokens, or private keys in PostgreSQL? [Traceability, Spec §NFR-006, Constitution §IX]
- [x] CHK051 Does the specification mandate that remote URLs containing embedded basic-auth credentials or tokens are rejected at registration with HTTP 422? [Security, Spec §FR-034, §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK052 Is ambient host authentication (host SSH keys/agent, system Git credential helper, or environment variables) explicitly defined as the sole authentication mechanism for private repositories in F01? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-006, §Clarifications]
- [x] CHK053 Are credential masking and sanitization requirements specified for all logging, error payloads, and API responses? [Security, Spec §SC-003, §NFR-006, §NFR-007]

## 12. Structured Logging & Observability

- [x] CHK054 Are structured logging requirements specified using `structlog` for all project and repository lifecycle operations? [Traceability, Spec §NFR-009, Constitution §XI]
- [x] CHK055 Are mandatory context fields specified for log events (including `project_id`, `repository_id`, `event`, and `timestamp`)? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-009]
- [x] CHK056 Are failed connectivity checks specified to emit logs at `WARNING` level with diagnostic failure reasons (and sanitized targets)? [Consistency, Spec §NFR-010]
- [x] CHK057 Is automatic credential redaction enforced across all log formatters in compliance with Phase 0 logging configuration? [Consistency, Spec §NFR-007, Phase 0 Architecture]

## 13. Configuration & Dependency Boundaries

- [x] CHK058 Are any new configuration parameters (e.g., Git command timeout, Git binary path) specified to integrate with `ApplicationConfig` via `pydantic-settings`, with zero default-branch fallback (prohibiting fabricated branch names)? [Consistency, Spec §NFR-005, Phase 0 Architecture]
- [x] CHK059 Does the specification enforce the 5-layer onion architecture: pure domain models in `trace/domain/` with ZERO external dependencies or I/O imports? [Traceability, Spec §NFR-005, Constitution Architecture Constraints]
- [x] CHK060 Does the specification require concrete Git adapters to be instantiated strictly at the lifespan composition root (`trace/main.py`), preventing direct instantiation in routers or domain services? [Consistency, Spec §NFR-005, Phase 0 Architecture]
- [x] CHK061 Does the specification explicitly prohibit any write operations, node creation, or schema definition in Neo4j during F01? [Traceability, Spec §NFR-004, Constitution §X]

## 14. Testing Specifications & Determinism

- [x] CHK063 Are unit test specifications defined for project and repository domain models, status transitions, and normalization logic? [Completeness, Spec §US1, §US2]
- [x] CHK064 Are service layer test specifications defined using test doubles / mocks for `DatabaseGateway` and `GitProvider`? [Completeness, Spec §NFR-013]
- [x] CHK065 Are persistence test specifications aligned with the Phase 0 test-double architecture, using `InMemoryDatabaseGateway` (the established SQLite in-memory test double) for unit/service tests and isolated PostgreSQL database fixtures for live integration and migration tests? [Completeness, Spec §NFR-001, §NFR-003]
- [x] CHK066 Are API contract test specifications defined covering all 10 F01 endpoints for positive (200/201/204) and negative (404/409/422/500) cases? [Coverage, Spec §FR-029, §FR-033]
- [x] CHK067 Are deterministic local Git test fixtures specified (creating temporary Git repos via `git init` in pytest fixtures)? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-012]
- [x] CHK068 Are remote Git validation tests specified using mock/stub `GitProvider` adapters to simulate success, timeout, and authentication failures? [Clarity, Spec §NFR-013]
- [x] CHK069 Are integration tests requiring live databases properly isolated with the `@pytest.mark.integration` marker per Phase 0 convention? [Consistency, Spec §NFR-011, Phase 0 Architecture]
- [x] CHK070 Is an overall test coverage threshold of at least 80% line and branch coverage explicitly mandated across all new F01 modules? [Measurability, Spec §NFR-014, Constitution §XVI]
